status: closed fixed expert-gradient-centering candidate; research goal active
assessment: Exact original-expert CE gradient subtraction did not improve the four-task pilot. Mean effect versus CE is -0.130885 percentage points, with forward +0.021086 and reverse -0.282855. It is below pure output KL in both orders, mean -0.194295 points. The sole positive task versus CE is Workload; deleting it gives -0.836443 points. No second bank or full16 expansion of this fixed candidate is justified by these results.
KL_control_assessment: Pure output KL is +0.063410 percentage points versus CE across two orders, but loses on FACED and turns negative when MI, ADHD or Workload is omitted. This is a small, task-sensitive existing-method control, not a new-method success.
diagnostic_scope: Median source-to-student gradient norm ratios in the centered runs are approximately 0.00909 forward and 0.00176 reverse. These are observed projected minibatch gradients under this affine merge parameterization, not proof of a general cause or universal small source gradients.
audit_status: Six workers and reporter exited successfully. Unchanged CE controls match the frozen reference native checkpoint hashes. All native exports independently reconstructed with maximum error at most 4.77e-7. No official test read.
next_action: Review source-training choices and exact algorithmic equivalences before selecting another runnable method. Do not launch source-aware training if it merely reparameterizes already-tested native fine-tuning, and do not treat generic merge-aware training as novel. Any selected method must have matched source and merge costs and causal arrival inputs.
scope: Four exposed development tasks,one original expert/calibration bank,two actual arrival orders. All arms compute identical per-batch frozen-original-expert CE gradients at the same arrived task. CE and KL controls discard those gradients. Source-centered fitting subtracts their exact pullback through the current affine bilateral merge family. Same student examples,optimizer updates,teacher forward/backward examples,and fixed checkpoint means. Training retains arrived expert active weights;inference uses one native checkpoint. No future expert payload,new source training,official test,novelty or superiority claim.
